A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HSD research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and visual inspection supports matching equations, tables, figures, and relocated content despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original parsing accuracy, acceleration measurements, component ablations, draft-quality perturbation tests, and qualitative examples across three benchmarks.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds model and baseline comparisons, parser latency measurements, and a computational-cost analysis.

M1.justification: The two-stage hierarchy, fixed pipeline drafts, window matching, and tree verification remain. However, v1 Equation (10) accepts using log p(best)/log p(candidate) >= tau, whereas v2 Equation (11) uses log p(candidate) - log p(best) >= log tau. These inequivalent conditions change the specified acceptance procedure locally; the PDFs do not establish whether implementations or experiments were correspondingly changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use OmniDocBench v1.5, olmOCR-Bench, and Ocean-OCR-Bench, retaining their document categories, English/Chinese coverage, and draft-degradation scenarios. Additional target models and comparisons do not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: V2 Table 4 adds evaluated Medusa and EAGLE-2 baselines to the retained VSD and official/task-adapted ViSpec comparisons. Its new Table 5 compares accelerated parsers against MinerU2-pipeline, PP-StructureV3, MonkeyOCR-pro-3B, and MinerU2.5 as complete parsing systems. This substantially broadens the comparator set beyond v1's speculative-decoding comparison and drafter analyses.

E3.justification: V2 introduces Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B configurations and comparisons using the same Qwen2.5-VL-3B target for HSD, Medusa, EAGLE-2, and ViSpec, with task-adapted drafters trained on the same document-parsing data. HunyuanOCR evaluation extends to the other two retained benchmarks. V1's explicit Qwen length-filtering conditions disappear, but this omission does not establish that filtering actually changed.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix B adds an analysis of FLOPs, arithmetic intensity, memory traffic, forward-pass counts, and Roofline-predicted latency. V1's Qwen length-bias/repetition analysis and separate VSD draft-generation-latency diagnostic disappear, although much of the 8192-token appendix data survives in v2's main tables. The stage/tolerance ablations, draft perturbation tests, and four qualitative case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Revised AAL and speedup values do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial model, baseline, parser-latency, and computational-cost results. Existing entries also change: dots.ocr's OmniDocBench AAL changes from 4.98 to 3.98 while its 2.42x speedup remains; Qwen3-VL-8B's Ocean-OCR end-to-end speedup changes from 6.09x to 3.70x, and Qwen3-VL-2B's English/Chinese entries are reversed. Tables 1–2 largely retain v1 Appendix A category scores with revised aggregate/AAL values. Unspecified filtering prevents interpreting these as same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: The acceptance inequality is substantively revised, rather than merely re-typeset: v1 implies p(candidate) >= p(best)^(1/tau), while v2 implies p(candidate) >= tau*p(best). Appendix B also introduces a Roofline calculation and predicted speedup. The remaining mathematical framework is equivalent, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central training-free, hierarchical acceleration contribution remains. The abstract and conclusion switch their headline from dots.ocr's 2.42x/4.89x to HunyuanOCR's 2.78x/7.04x, already present in v1 Table 1, and qualify acceleration as near-lossless. V2 also removes the explicit claim of being the first work to introduce speculative decoding into document parsing.

C2.justification: V2 adds a memory-bandwidth/Roofline explanation and interprets the new parser comparison as achieving hybrid-level efficiency. It removes the substantive Qwen repetition/length-bias caveat and engineering limitations concerning attention kernels, tree processing, and memory management. Existing draft-quality and prefill bottleneck explanations remain; Appendix C largely reiterates the existing rationale for global verification.

D1.justification: V2 adds A100 80GB SXM hardware specifications for the Roofline analysis and describes shared-data adaptation of comparison drafters. It removes the explicit 2048/8192-token filtering and repetition-exclusion disclosures. Transformers, FlexAttention, PP-StructureV3, n=3, tau=0.75, and the future code-release promise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including Qwen2.5-VL, Sparrow, and Roofline work, while removing references associated with degeneration analysis and some engineering discussion. It withdraws the explicit first-use novelty claim and emphasizes global coherence relative to hybrid parsers. The related-work taxonomy largely remains; the Qwen3-VL repository-to-report substitution concerns the same model family.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological explanations, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around HSD and global coherence. Windowed alignment becomes draft–target matching, draft-quality discussion moves into the ablation section, and the appendix organization changes. These are broad editorial and structural revisions beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column to a single-column layout. Figure 1 adds explicit error/correction highlighting, Figure 2 rearranges its panels, and Figure 3 merges three perturbation plots into one. Table 4 gains target-model and multi-benchmark structure; the draft-latency table is replaced by a parser comparison. The repetition figure disappears, while the four retained qualitative figures are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The same-target baseline comparisons address an acknowledged weakness in v1, and the clearer hierarchy explanation and new computational-cost analysis strengthen the paper. However, Qwen filtering disclosures disappear despite extensive reuse of v1's filtered appendix results. V2 also introduces unresolved inconsistencies: Table 5 gives dots.ocr baseline accuracy as 86.73 versus 88.41 in Table 7, and Table 8's AAL values disagree with its accompanying prose. These gains coexist with reduced evaluation transparency and numerical ambiguity, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
